purpose: A workbench for evaluating, designing, and describing agentic AI systems — tools, harnesses, loops, workflows, and orchestration frameworks. Single-purpose, client-side, zero accounts. Statuses, caveats, and estimates are stated honestly: planned tools are not counted as shipped, duplicates are flagged, and no tool claims capabilities it does not have.

dimensions.label: Reliability
dimensions.description: Deterministic behavior, repeatability, stable long-run execution, graceful degradation, clear rollback paths.

dimensions.label: Architecture & Contracts
dimensions.description: Schemas, interfaces, domain rules, module boundaries, separation of responsibilities.

dimensions.label: Closed-loop Evaluation
dimensions.description: Automated scoring, feedback cycles, error clustering, traceability, continuous improvement.

dimensions.label: Tooling Integration
dimensions.description: Explicit I/O contracts, retries, rate limits, secure action boundaries, extensibility.

dimensions.label: Workflow & Orchestration
dimensions.description: Planning, acting, evaluating, branching, async execution, parallelism, deterministic handoffs.

dimensions.label: Observability
dimensions.description: Distributed tracing, decision logs, cost monitoring, drift detection, transparency into agent reasoning.

dimensions.label: Safety & Governance
dimensions.description: Budget caps, forbidden actions, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, output validation, compliance boundaries.

dimensions.label: Scale & Maintainability
dimensions.description: Modular architecture, versioning, CI/CD compatibility, reproducibility, low operational overhead.

focuses.evaluate: Evaluate: benchmarks, evals, judges, and diagnostics
focuses.design: Design: harnesses, schemas, context & state engineering
focuses.operate: Operate: cost, capacity, latency, and proxy infrastructure

apps.name: Meter Shock
apps.description: Projects usage-based spend to month-end from today's burn rate and flags the day you cross budget, with a 7-day trailing velocity check, cost per task, and blended $/M.

apps.name: Pipeline Rot
apps.description: Scores an ML/data pipeline against measured decay patterns — drift, step changes, volatility, staleness, missing data — with a weighted rot score and recommendations. Real statistics computed from your timeline, nothing fabricated.

apps.name: Zombie Stack
apps.description: Tracks services and subscriptions by last-active date, flags zombies past an idle threshold, and totals wasted spend per month and year. Ledger persists in localStorage; CSV export.

apps.name: AI Infra Router & SOW Generator
apps.description: Deterministic build-vs-buy decision framework (data sovereignty, volume, latency → topology), a rough GPU-vs-API cost comparison, a client-side email/IP scrubber, and a templated statement of work.
apps.notes: The cost model is an unlabeled rough estimate and the generated SOW is template text stamped 'APPROVED ARCHITECTURAL SPECIFICATION' — treat as scaffolding for a conversation, not as numbers or a document of record.

apps.name: Model Latency & Cost Profiler
apps.description: Cost math per provider tier: monthly spend, blended $/M, configurable input/output split and custom rates, plus typical TTFT/token-speed estimates and an SLA-compliance flag.
apps.notes: The directory id (jeff-dean-latency-capacity-profiler) and the originally advertised 'Jeff Dean capacity calculator' are legacy/misleading — this tool is the cost & latency profiler, and the capacity calculator was never built. TTFT/token-speed are canned estimates, not measurements.

apps.name: Model Latency & Cost Profiler (legacy duplicate)
apps.description: Older copy of the latency/cost profiler: Gemini 1.5-era pricing, hardcoded 75/25 input/output split, and a $500 efficiency threshold. Kept for reference only.
apps.notes: Superseded by the canonical profiler (jeff-dean-latency-capacity-profiler entry). Listed so the registry never hides what exists on disk.

apps.name: Agent Hedge Request Tester
apps.description: Monte Carlo simulation comparing plain vs speculative-hedged requests on P50/P99 tail latency, and reporting the extra-request overhead %. Transparently a model — useful for understanding the hedging trade-off, not production numbers.
apps.notes: No cancellation or correlated-failure modeling; percentiles are index approximations.

apps.name: EdgeGuard AI
apps.description: Dual-engine inference router: primary Groq call raced against a Gemini Flash fallback fired at a 250 ms hedge threshold, with real API calls from your browser.
apps.notes: Known bug: the hedge timer is never cleared and the losing request is never aborted, so any hedged run double-bills tokens. Do not use as-is in production.

apps.name: AI Engineering Tool Suite (this hub)
apps.description: The registry hub itself, rendered from the same apps.json as the root index with focus, dimension, status, and mode filters. One source of truth; no duplicate metadata.

apps.name: Context Budgeting & Compactor
apps.description: Keep-newest-lines-within-token-budget compaction for prompts, chats, and agent memory, with a rough token estimate (words × 1.33). It trims — it does not summarize or prioritize semantically.
apps.notes: Token counts are heuristic estimates (words × 1.33), not model tokenizers.

apps.name: ReAct Loop Visualizer
apps.description: Parses Thought → Action → Observation trace lines into a color-coded, step-through timeline for inspecting intermediate agent loop steps and spotting stuck loops.

apps.name: MCP Client Inspector
apps.description: Recursively compiles MCP-style tool definitions into OpenAI-style function schemas or Gemini FunctionDeclarations as you type, handling nested objects/arrays, enums, defaults, and required flags.
apps.notes: The Gemini branch drops enums and mishandles array-of-object; input is a custom JSON shape, not raw MCP tool definitions.

apps.name: Multi-LLM Arena & Parallel Tester
apps.description: Fires one prompt at two models in parallel (Gemini + Groq), measuring true streaming TTFT, total latency, tok/s, trigram-dice output similarity, and an LCS diff. Clearly-labeled simulation mode without keys.

apps.name: LLM-as-a-Judge Rubric Evaluator
apps.description: Grades output against your own rubric via a live Gemini judge (weighted scores with rationale), plus an honest local structural-check mode that refuses to fake rubric grades.

apps.name: Needle in a Haystack Benchmarker
apps.description: Real retrieval sweep: embeds a needle at each context depth, queries the model, and produces a depth-recall curve with a lost-in-the-middle diagnosis. Local mode validates the harness but never fabricates recall numbers.
apps.notes: Filler corpus is 20 sentences repeated; answer matching is substring-based.

apps.name: System Prompt Mutation Optimizer
apps.description: Generates deterministic prompt variants (negative constraints, delimiters, structure, compression, output format, persona) and ranks them via transparent local heuristics or a live judge leaderboard.
apps.notes: The local score is a weighted regex checklist — an exploration aid, not a rigorous metric.

apps.name: Agentic HITL Gatekeeper
apps.description: Policy gate for agent tool calls: regex classification auto-blocks destructive payloads, auto-approves read-only ones, and escalates mutations to a human override. Rules run locally on the payload's actual content.
apps.notes: Regex classification is brittle — a payload containing 'get_' or 'SELECT' anywhere is classified read-only. Use for prototyping policy semantics, not as a security boundary.

apps.name: Golden Dataset Test Harness
apps.description: Golden-set regression runner: JSON/CSV ingest, honest local dataset lint (duplicate IDs, missing expected outputs, key coverage), then live parallel runs against Gemini with deep-diff comparison and per-case latency.

apps.name: Adversarial Edge-Case Red-Teamer
apps.description: Generates four canned attack strings (instruction override, prompt extraction, obfuscated payload, roleplay breakout) and rates prompt hardening by regex. It does not execute attacks or test a model.
apps.notes: The vulnerability rating is two regex tests over the prompt text — a checklist, not a security audit. Do not treat its LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH as evidence of real robustness.

apps.name: Few-Shot Canonical Example Builder
apps.description: Formats a JSON array of input/output exemplar pairs into a copy-paste few-shot prompt block with a rough token budget. Formatting only — it does not optimize or tokenize.

apps.name: Context Compression Benchmarker
apps.description: Compresses your actual text with gzip (lossless), keep-newest trimming, and dedup+stopword stripping; measures real ratios and lexical retention. Optional live LLM summary row with a key.

apps.name: Multi-Agent GAN Contract Evaluator
apps.description: Validates a JSON payload against the required-key list of a schema contract and reports missing keys. That is the entire check.
apps.notes: Schema type fields are never validated; there is no recursion and no critique loop. The GAN/discriminator framing overstates a required-key presence check.

apps.name: Edge Exponential Backoff Gateway
apps.description: Seeded discrete-event simulation of a token-bucket rate limiter with jittered exponential backoff (full/equal/none) vs an unlimited baseline — 429s, retries, failures, wall-time, throughput, and p95.

apps.name: Scratchpad State Manager
apps.description: Wraps agent scratchpad state into a versioned hand-off payload with a real SHA-256 integrity hash (WebCrypto) and a verify path. Runs fully locally.
apps.notes: The hash is keyless — it detects accidental corruption, not malicious tampering.

apps.name: JSON Schema Repair Loop
apps.description: Was advertised as validating outputs against JSON Schemas and running targeted auto-repair iteration loops.
apps.notes: Advertised in the original registry but never shipped — the link 404s on the live site. Listed as roadmap; do not link to it until built.

apps.name: Context Firewall & Hand-off Generator
apps.description: Was advertised as stripping trace noise from agent chats and building compact, redacted state hand-off payloads.
apps.notes: Advertised in the original registry but never shipped — the link 404s on the live site. Listed as roadmap; do not link to it until built.
